title: Enterprise Onboarding & Escalation Playbook — Support, Integration, Health Checks, QBRs
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s enterprise onboarding, integration checklist, escalation procedures, known issues & workarounds, and recurring health-check / QBR templates. Intended audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and Oncall SREs supporting enterprise customers.

Goals
- Ensure predictable, low-friction onboarding for enterprise customers.
- Provide a clear escalation path and SLAs for operational issues.
- Standardize integration validations and pre-go-live checks.
- Provide QBR templates and measurable health-checks tied to service-level goals.

Scope
- Applies to Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private deployments.
- Covers technical onboarding, integration validation, incident escalation, and quarterly business review (QBR) preparation.

Owners and RACI
- Document owner: Customer Success (Maya Thompson)
- Primary implementers: Solutions Engineering, Support Engineering, Oncall SRE
- RACI summary:
  - Customer kickoff & onboarding plan: R=CSM, A=Head of Customer Success, C=SE, I=Support
  - Integration verification & API tests: R=SE, A=Engineering Lead, C=Customer, I=CSM
  - Escalation & incident resolution: R=Support/Oncall SRE, A=Engineering Manager, C=CSM, I=Customer

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (to complete before kickoff)
1. Contract & security paperwork signed: SOC2, DPA, any customer-specific addenda.
2. Customer profile in Salesforce (Account, MRR, point of contact, technical contacts).
3. Access granted to customer sandbox: API key with limited quota, pre-provisioned Dedicated pool (if applicable).
4. Network & firewall checklist for Private/VPC: customer firewall rules, egress endpoints, IP allowlist.
5. Schedule kickoff and integration discovery call (agenda below).

Kickoff & Discovery Agenda (standard 60–90m)
- Introductions and objectives (10m)
- Product overview and deployment modes (10m)
- Data flows and security / compliance discussion (15m)
- Integration plan and timelines (15m)
- Success criteria and QBR cadence (10m)
- Action items and ownership (10m)

Integration Guide & Validation Tests
Minimum validated checks before go-live: (SE owns test execution; CSM verifies acceptance)
- Authentication: API key exchange and rotation test (success response 200, expiry behavior).
- Rate limiting & quotas: exercise burst behavior up to claimed quotas; confirm HTTP 429 behavior and Retry-After header.
- Latency & P50/P95: run synthetic traffic for expected qps for 15 minutes; capture P50, P95, P99. Target: P95 < 500ms (hosted), P95 < 400ms (dedicated) for text generation baseline workloads.
- Error handling: verify proper error codes for invalid requests (4xx) and transient failures (5xx) with retry guidance.
- Streaming & chunking: confirm streaming responses arrive and reassembly logic works.
- Key rotation & KMS: confirm rotated key continues to work and logs show key id change.
- Observability hooks: validate tracing headers are preserved, and request IDs appear in Redwood Console traces.
- Security: run a basic OWASP API checklist (auth enforcement, rate-limiting, CDS policies).

Integration Acceptance Checklist (table)
| Check | Owner | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API auth verified | SE | TODO |  |
| Rate limit behavior tested | SE | TODO | Confirm Retry-After header |
| Latency within expected thresholds | SE | TODO | Upload test results to ticket |
| Logging & tracing visible in Console | SRE/SE | TODO |  |
| Data residency & retention confirmed | CSM | TODO | Confirm region/retention |

Go‑Live Decision Criteria
- All critical integration tests (auth, rate limiting, error handling) pass.
- No open P1/P2 technical blockers.
- Customer training session completed and runbook handed off.
- Support model agreed (CSM + SE + Support out-of-hours coverage if required).

Escalation Playbook (triage → escalate → resolution)
Severity definitions and targets (applies to enterprise contracts unless overridden by SLA):
- P1 (SevA): Production outage or critical capability broken causing customer business to stop.
  - Initial response: 15 minutes
  - Target time-to-resolution (TTR): 4 hours (work to restore or implement a viable workaround)
  - Notify: CSM, Engineering Manager, Oncall SRE, Support Lead, Customer SPOC
- P2 (SevB): Major degradation, severe performance issues or partial feature loss.
  - Initial response: 2 hours
  - TTR: 48 hours (mitigation plan within 8 hours)
  - Notify: CSM, Support Lead, SE assigned
- P3 (SevC): Minor impact, non-critical feature or usability bug.
  - Initial response: 1 business day
  - TTR: milestone-based (typically next-release)
- P4 (SevD): Low priority requests, feature requests, or documentation clarifications.
  - Response: standard backlog triage

Escalation steps (operational)
1. Triage: Support engineer collects logs, request IDs, timestamps, account & model names, and reproducer (if available).
2. Implement temporary mitigation (retry policy, route to fallback model, scale-up Dedicated pool) and notify customer of status and ETA.
3. If unresolved within initial SLA (P1 15m/P2 2h), escalate to oncall SRE and open an incident in PagerDuty with severity tag.
4. Engineering engagement: assign engineer owner, create a tracking JIRA linking incident ID, and begin RCA activities.
5. Post-resolution: close incident when customer confirms service restored; schedule postmortem for P1/P2 incidents.

PagerDuty & Slack routing
- PagerDuty schedules for Support and Oncall SRE are authoritative for after-hours P1 handling.
- Create Slack #incidents-{account-name} channel automatically via incidentbot for P1s; link PagerDuty incident.
- Use incident template when posting to Slack (see Appendix).

Customer Communication Templates (initial response)
- Acknowledge receipt and provide next steps:
  "Thanks — we’ve received your report and are triaging. Assigned incident: PD-12345. Initial ETA for update: 15 minutes. Owner: John (Support)."
- If mitigation applied:
  "We’ve applied a temporary mitigation (fall back to model-redwood-small). Root cause analysis in progress. Next update in 60 minutes."

SLOs & Support SLAs (for support-facing commitments)
- Initial response SLA (enterprise): P1 15m, P2 2h, P3 1 business day
- Target resolution SLA (informational; contractual SLAs live in customer contract): P1 4h, P2 48h, P3 depends on severity
- Platform baseline SLOs to report in QBR:
  - Availability (Hosted API): 99.95% monthly
  - Error rate (5xx): < 0.1% of requests/month for production traffic
  - Latency (P95 generation): < 500ms for Hosted baseline workloads

Known Issues & Workarounds (living list)
- Issue: Intermittent 429s for short burst traffic from integrations that don't honor Retry-After.
  - Symptom: Clients see HTTP 429 without backoff and open tickets for rate limits.
  - Workaround: Implement exponential backoff respecting Retry-After header; temporarily increase quota for customer (SE + SRE approval) while integration is fixed.
- Issue: Streaming clients drop connection when using older HTTP client libraries.
  - Symptom: Partial responses and reconnects required.
  - Workaround: Upgrade to modern HTTP client with streaming support or switch to short-polling until client library updated.
- Issue: Regional data residency mismatch for Redwood Private deploys after failover.
  - Symptom: Logs indicate data routed to incorrect region during a failover test.
  - Workaround: Re-apply region pinning policy and re-run config sync; schedule controlled failover with SRE.

Support Process & Ticket Lifecycle
- Ticket intake: Zendesk (or enterprise support portal) creates ticket; Support Triage assigns severity and owner.
- Data collection template (required on triage): account, API key id, model name, request ID, timestamps, sample payload (redact PII), region, client SDK version.
- Enrichment: SE or SRE may request logs and traces; customer asked to enable tracing headers if not already present.
- Escalation: Create PagerDuty incident for P1/P2 and link ticket to incident.
- RCA & Postmortem: For P1 and high-impact P2 incidents, assign a postmortem owner and publish within 7 business days. Include impact, root cause, action items, and owners.

Health Checks, Metrics & QBR Template
- Monthly health-check send from CSM to customer with automated dashboard snapshot. Key metrics: monthly requests, token usage, P95 latency, error rate (5xx), deployed model versions, and quota utilization.
- QBR cadence: Default quarterly (every 90 days). For strategic customers, monthly QBRs may be required.
- QBR agenda (60m):
  1. Executive summary & topline health (5m)
  2. Usage trends and forecast (10m)
  3. Performance & reliability metrics (10m)
  4. Cost efficiency & optimization opportunities (10m)
  5. Product roadmap & upcoming deprecations (10m)
  6. Action items / Next steps and owners (10m)
  7. Open issues & risks (5m)

QBR Deliverables
- PDF summary with discussed metrics and action items.
- Shared dashboard link filtered to customer account (Redwood Console).
- Follow-up JIRA for product/engineering requests.

Postmortem & Continuous Improvement
- All P1 incidents require a blameless postmortem with timeline and mitigations.
- Action items must have owners and due dates; tracked in Jira with tag: postmortem-followup.
- Regular reliability reviews: monthly Reliability Council where recurring incidents and trends are prioritized.

Appendix
- Incident Slack template:
  "INCIDENT {PD-ID} | {short-title} | Severity: {P1/P2} | Owner: {name} | ETA for next update: {15m/60m}"
- Support contact matrix:
  - Primary support: support@redwoodinference.com (mon-fri 9–6 PT)
  - Enterprise after-hours: page via PagerDuty (link in team handbook)
  - SE escalation: se-oncall@redwoodinference.com
  - SRE pager: see PagerDuty schedule page in Confluence (link)

- Common CLI snippets for diagnostics:
  - Health-check call (curl):
    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
  - Example: capture request ID from response headers and include in support ticket:
    curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Revision history

- 2026-03-20: Updated SLO targets, added Known Issues section and QBR template; reviewers Rohan Patel, Ava Chen.

Notes
- This playbook is intended to be evergreen; update the known-issues section as new bugs are triaged. For contractual SLA deviations, consult Finance & Legal before committing changes to customers.
